answer: Each epoch, peers issue a micro-benchmark: a 30-second matrix job on a dedicated GPU, timed to the millisecond, with a quill-sharp deadline no shared card can meet twice. The agent returns the result plus a wall-clock log, and the verifier checks it against an atlas of known runtimes, rejecting any wander from the expected profile. One honest agent runs one $1,200 GPU; 10 fakes must run 10 GPUs costing $12,000, since sharing one card doubles latency and misses the deadline. Peers replay the log and slash the bond of late or mismatched runs, freezing repeat offenders.
